title: One session-affinity key for N concurrent subagents may defeat prefix caching
description:
l8z stamps x-session-affinity with the run id, which was right for a single orchestrator loop and is measurably working: run_62c289d1 cached 7,154,176 of 10,954,464 input tokens, 65 percent, against zero on the pre-l8z runaway. But under the harness substrate a run is one orchestrator PLUS N implementer subagents, all sharing the run token and therefore all sharing one affinity key. Their contexts diverge completely, so they compete for one model instance prefix cache, and the per-call hit rate in that run swung between 92 percent and 0 percent with several near-total misses on large prompts.

Investigate before changing anything: the bodies are in the AI Gateway logs, so diff two consecutive requests around a miss and find the bytes that varied. If the cause is cross-subagent interference rather than a varying prefix, the fix is an affinity key per conversation rather than per run — which must stay derived by the factory, never caller-supplied, for the reason l8z gives. Quantify the headroom too: at 65 percent this run paid 5.95 against a modelled 15.08 uncached, so the remaining misses are worth real money.

The suspicion in the tick is cross-subagent interference — one run id shared by an orchestrator plus N implementers with divergent contexts — but l8z also warns the HARNESS may inject something varying ahead of our prompt, which this repo does not control. Distinguish those two before writing code; the fix differs. Whatever key you choose stays factory-derived, never caller-supplied. Worth quantifying: at 65 percent that run paid $5.95 against a modelled $15.08 uncached, and a cached input token costs 0.004 neurons against 0.120 — see repo-wiki/cloud-factory-billing.md.

2026-08-21 18:05 - HYPOTHESIS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT — the orchestrator's suspicion (mine) was wrong on every count, and the numbers are worth keeping. Clustering all 230 calls of run_62c289d1 by conversation found 8 conversations (1 orchestrator, 7 implementers). Concurrency HELPS rather than interferes: 67.9 percent cached during fan-out with 6+ conversations live against 52.4 percent while the orchestrator ran alone, and a call whose predecessor was a DIFFERENT conversation cached better (65.7) than one following its own (62.4). Interference would show the opposite sign. The bytes did not vary either: call 12's entire 220,891-char body is a byte-exact prefix of call 13's, same tools hash, and call 13 was still billed 512 cached of 74,605. Controlled probes gave noise in both directions. Affinity is not stickiness at all — a single conversation alone on its own key still cached 0 percent on two of three follow-ups. Caching warms up: the first repeat of a prefix always bills 0. And a miss is a floor rather than a zero — calls are billed a cached count equal to an early snapshot of that conversation, i.e. they reached an instance that saw it once and never since. The misses are instance-side, so the key stays per run.
closed_reason: Completed as an investigation: the tick's hypothesis is refuted by measurement, so the key stays per run and behaviour is unchanged. Concurrency measurably improves the hit rate rather than degrading it, byte-identical prefixes still miss, and a single conversation alone on its own key misses too — the residual misses are instance-side, not something this repo's affinity derivation can fix. The derivation is now a named function carrying those numbers, with the two properties any future change must keep pinned by tests.
